claims.statement: Tom Allen and Joe Goss signed articles at the Empire Saloon in Cincinnati to fight under the new London Prize Ring rules for $5,000 ($2,500 a side).
claims.excerpt: to meet in a twenty-four-foot ring and fight, under the new rules of the London Prize Ring, for the sum of five thousand doilars

claims.statement: The Allen and Goss fight was set for September 7, 1876, at a place within one hundred miles of Cincinnati to be chosen by Ephraim Holland.
claims.excerpt: September sev-enth Gt), 1876, they will meet ata point, to be selected by

claims.statement: Ben De Bar stood by Tom Allen at the signing and put up Allen's money.
claims.excerpt: was Ben De Bar, ready to. put up necéssary money

claims.statement: Tom Allen and Joe Goss were bound over before 'Squire Anthony not to break the peace in Ohio for one year.
claims.excerpt: and bound themselves not to break the peace in the State of Ohio for one year.

fights.notes: Articles signed in Cincinnati, May 12, 1876; the fight was not yet held. The 'Thursday' in the hint is not in the text. The date is printed as 'sof September seventh'.

notes: Articles of agreement reprinted from the Cincinnati Commercial. The hint's 'challenge' is recorded here as an agreed match, so it is a fight.
